Official character design turnaround sheet for an original anime music video heroine named DOT. Modern TV-anime key-art style: crisp confident black lineart, flat two-tone cel shading with one hard shadow tone, clean shapes, no gradients, no painterly texture, bright even studio lighting, plain very light warm-gray background. Layout: four full-body views in a row (front, three-quarter, side profile, back) standing in a relaxed neutral pose at identical scale, plus a row of three head close-ups: singing with mouth open wide on an "ah" vowel, soft hopeful smile, determined gaze looking up.
DOT is a 20-year-old East Asian young woman, slim athletic dancer build, long straight glossy jet-black hair to mid-back with blunt bangs and a hidden pale sky-blue under-layer that shows when the hair moves, large dark-brown eyes with a small pale-blue ring highlight. She wears chunky white over-ear studio headphones with orange ear cups resting around her neck, an oversized cropped white technical bomber jacket with a bright orange reflective stripe across the chest and two round embroidered patches (a tiny pale blue dot on black; the text "1420 MHz"), a black ribbed high-neck crop top, loose dark navy wide-leg cargo pants with orange utility straps, and chunky white sneakers. In the full-body views she holds a small handheld Yagi antenna (thin aluminum rods on a boom, orange grip) at her side.
Consistent face, hair, outfit and proportions across every view. Character sheet, model sheet, reference sheet.

Official character model sheet for DOT, the heroine of an original anime music video about searching the sky for a signal from another civilization. Premium modern anime key-art style (Trigger / Science SARU / KPop-idol-anime energy): crisp confident black lineart with varied line weight, flat cel shading with exactly one hard shadow tone, clean graphic shapes, no gradients, no painterly texture, even studio lighting, plain very light warm-gray background, small clean sans-serif labels.
LAYOUT: top row = four full-body views at identical scale (FRONT, THREE-QUARTER, SIDE, BACK) standing relaxed; bottom row = four head-and-shoulders expressions (SINGING "AH" with mouth wide open, SINGING "OO" with rounded lips, CLOSED-EYE HOPEFUL SMILE, FIERCE DETERMINED LOOKING UP) plus two prop callouts (HEADPHONES, YAGI ANTENNA).
DOT: 20-year-old East Asian woman, slim athletic dancer build. Hair: long straight glossy jet-black "hime cut" — blunt eyebrow-length bangs, cheek-length side locks framing the face, the rest to mid-back — with a hidden pale sky-blue under-layer that flashes when the hair moves. Eyes: large, dark brown, each with one round pale-blue dot-shaped catchlight (her signature). Headphones: retro 1977-style lightweight headphones with thin silver headband and round bright orange foam ear pads, worn around her neck. Jacket: oversized cropped white technical flight jacket, bright orange reflective stripe across the chest and sleeves, a small round patch with a tiny pale-blue dot on the left chest, a round patch reading "1420 MHz" on the right sleeve; on the BACK of the jacket one large solid pale-blue circle (the "pale blue dot") with tiny text "RARE EARTH" beneath it. Black ribbed high-neck crop top, loose dark-navy wide-leg cargo pants with orange utility straps, chunky white sneakers. Prop: a small handheld Yagi antenna (five thin aluminum rods on a slim boom, orange rubber grip) held low in her right hand.
Keep face, hair, outfit, colors and proportions perfectly consistent across every view.

Art-direction style board titled "SIGNAL PRINT — visual language for the RARE EARTH music video". A clean, confident graphic-design presentation board on warm off-white paper, Swiss-grid layout, small monospace annotations.
The style: a moving risograph / screen-printed anime. Every image is built from a few flat spot-color inks with crisp black ink linework, halftone-dot shading, slight color misregistration, and paper grain; when the signal is strong the print "lights up" into glowing neon linework on black.
Board contents:
1) INK PALETTE as round swatches with names and hex codes: KLEIN BLUE #1F2BD1 (Earth night), BEACON ORANGE #FF5A1F (Earth warmth, aviation lights), PALE BLUE DOT #9CCBFF (Earth, DOT), FLUO PINK #FF48B0 (the other world's sky), MINT SIGNAL #3FE0C5 (the other world's lights), SIGNAL YELLOW #FFE14D (contact), INK #0B0B14, PAPER #F3EFE6.
2) Four sample frames in 16:9 thumbnails:
 a) EARTH — an anime girl with long black hime-cut hair and orange foam headphones stands on top of a red-and-white radio antenna tower poking out of a sea of fog at night, raising a small handheld Yagi antenna to one star; printed in Klein blue + beacon orange + pale blue on paper, halftone fog.
 b) THE OTHER WORLD — a vast magenta sky with a giant planetary ring arcing overhead, a huge coral sun, a thin luminous space elevator rising from a terraced city; printed in fluo pink + mint + ink.
 c) LIGHT MODE — the same girl singing, drawn only as glowing mint and yellow neon outlines on pure black with bloom and speed lines.
 d) DATA INSERT — brutalist black-on-paper dot-matrix printout with the characters "6EQUJ5" circled in red pen, a transit light-curve graph with a small dip, and the word "LISTENING".
3) TYPE specimens: huge heavy extended grotesk lyric "DO YOU STILL CARE?", a condensed serif anime title card "RARE EARTH", monospace UI line "RX 1420.40575 MHz  SNR 23.4", Korean "희귀한 지구" and Japanese "どこかで、つながってる。" in bold display.
4) TEXTURE chips: coarse halftone dots, fine risograph grain, two-color misregistration, 1-bit dither, scanlines.

Environment design sheet for "ETZ-1715 b", an inhabited alien world in an anime sci-fi music video — shown only at architectural and planetary scale, no creatures or people visible anywhere. Style: premium anime background art (Makoto Shinkai skies meets Moebius clean line and flat color), crisp, luminous, graphic.
The world: a super-Earth orbiting a large coral-orange star. Magenta-to-violet sky, a bright planetary ring arcing across the whole sky, violet-black vegetation, pale mint-teal bioluminescent city lights.
Sheet panels (labeled with small clean captions):
1) HERO VISTA — at golden hour, a terraced cliff city of stacked white ring-shaped buildings with mint lights, a perfectly straight luminous space elevator tether rising from the city into the sky past the ring, climber cars glowing along it, huge coral sun low on the horizon.
2) THE LISTENING FIELD — a vast plain covered with hundreds of flower-like radio dishes (each dish made of six white petals that can open and close), arranged in a hexagonal grid, all tilted toward one point in the night sky.
3) FROM ORBIT — the planet's night side seen from space: city lights form clean hexagonal lattices and long glowing lines, an orbital ring of stations circling the planet, the thin space elevator line.
4) THEIR SIGNAL TOWER — a tall slender white tower rising above a sea of violet clouds, topped by a ring of pulsing mint lights.
5) SKY STUDY — night sky with the ring, two small moons, and one faint pale-blue star labeled "SOL".

Environment design sheet for the Earth locations of an anime sci-fi music video set in San Francisco and at a radio observatory. Style: premium anime background art (Makoto Shinkai light, clean line, flat graphic color), crisp and luminous, no people.
Panels with small clean captions:

2) THE ARRAY — a high-desert valley at night with forty-two white six-meter radio dishes on pedestals in a loose grid, all pointed at the same patch of the Milky Way, volcanic mountain silhouette behind.
3) NIGHT SHIFT — a cozy small radio-observatory control room at 3 a.m.: dark room, several monitors showing blue waterfall spectrograms and a single bright vertical line, a desk with coffee, headphones, sticky notes, a window showing a dish outside under stars.
4) LAUNCH — a giant stainless-steel rocket on a launch tower with huge mechanical catch arms at a coastal launch site at blue hour, steam venting.
5) PALE BLUE DOT — a vertical beam of scattered sunlight in black space with one tiny pale blue speck inside it.
